when: Acceptance depends on a check outside the producer claim.
reason: Evidence identity and acceptance authority are distinct questions.
limit: Evidence presence alone does not establish independent control.

when: A failed step can be located but its cause remains uncertain.
reason: A specific record supports testing one causal hypothesis.
limit: An obvious deterministic defect may need only a focused fix and regression.

when: The observed risk involves credentials or excessive capability.
reason: Credential boundaries and effective rights address different mechanisms.
limit: One successful refusal cannot establish all secrets or rights clauses.

when: An unattended run has effective action and duration boundaries.
reason: The run needs appropriate rights before its stop limit is reached.
limit: Neither a time cap nor a sandbox substitutes for the other test.

when: A change is being split and concurrent execution is considered.
reason: Reviewable size does not establish independent parallel parts.
limit: Do not add concurrency when the shared assumptions cannot be separated.

when: A worker lacks or ignores needed information.
reason: Task-specific sources and persistent repository rules have different scopes.
limit: Do not add permanent prose for every one-off omission.

when: Long work requires context renewal and execution limits.
reason: Session handover and enforced run termination solve different problems.
limit: Restarting a session does not establish cancellation or credential revocation.

when: Acceptance behavior includes an integration or real dependency transition.
reason: A local regression and a real-path rehearsal provide different observations.
limit: Do not claim all changes require the same broad end-to-end test.

when: A larger task needs an approved plan before execution.
reason: A plan needs a stated problem and completion condition to organize work.
limit: This procedure does not invent plan approval or redefine either test.

when: Untrusted content can influence a privileged action.
reason: Safe handling at a sink and mapping content-to-capability paths have different scopes.
limit: Preserve ae-015 applicability; ordinary generated source code is not automatically sink-bound output.

when: An agent reported done and the result fails.
reason: Evidence before done asks whether the done claim carried evidence tied to the acceptance criteria; Trace the run asks where the run went wrong, checked against a record the agent could not write.
limit: Both can be missing at once; evidence for the claim does not locate the failure, and a located failure does not repair the claim.

when: A change has been reviewed carefully and is about to merge.
reason: Review the diff is about what the review reads; Independent gates is about who gives the merge verdict and whether the agent can change, skip or pass it.
limit: A careful review does not make the acceptance independent, and an independent gate does not read the change.
